body:
Found in the second review of #863.

`data/ingredients/mapped/Na2hpo4_X_7_H2o.yaml` has the local identity `kgmicrobe.compound:na2hpo4_x_7_h2o`. It was minted on 2026-08-13 under MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 step 3, which covers "no exact term and no CAS". The record now carries `cas_rn: 7782-85-6`, the heptahydrate's own CAS. The x3 and x6 sibling records that shared it in the #334 scramble no longer carry it, and #863's unified snapshot publishes it on the `Na2HPO4·7H2O` row.

§3 step 2 says that when there is no exact term but the substance has its own CAS, `identifier` should be `cas:<its own CAS>`, with a broadMatch to the nearest parent and the Rule B1 registry row. Open semantic-review finding SEM:cb9ec35166086d936f70 already asks for "exact CAS promotion" on this record.

**Coupling with #863.** #863 adds a rejection-ledger row keyed (`kgmicrobe.compound:na2hpo4_x_7_h2o`, CHEBI:34683). A promotion to `cas:7782-85-6` must update that row's `mim_id` in the same change. Otherwise claw's `load_mapping_rejections` fails closed with "rejection disagrees with MIM identity".

**To do:**
1. Verify 7782-85-6 against an authoritative source for disodium hydrogen phosphate heptahydrate.
2. If it is confirmed, promote the record under §3 step 2 through the SSSOM receipt chain, update the ledger row in the same commit, and rebuild the unified snapshot.

comments.body:
The focused identity audit found an exact ontology term, so §3 step 1 takes precedence over the CAS fallback proposed in this issue: **NCIT:C61946 — Sodium Phosphate, Dibasic, Heptahydrate**. The inspected NCI EVS record is active in NCIt 26.10d and explicitly gives CAS 7782-85-6, formula `2Na.HO4P.7H2O`, and FDA UNII `70WT22SF4B`. [NCI EVS record](https://api-evsrest.nci.nih.gov/api/v1/concept/ncit/C61946?include=full); [FDA UNII record](https://precision.fda.gov/uniisearch/srs/unii/70WT22SF4B).

PubChem resolves the CAS to CID 6096963 and supplies the complete seven-water formula `H15Na2O11P`, mass 268.07, and hydrate-specific structure. The current YAML InChI/SMILES instead match the anhydrous CHEBI:34683 bytes. Whole-form identity and the anhydrous parent must remain distinct; a retained parent/component annotation needs its own supported non-identity representation. The structure correction remains a separate scope from the primary-identity decision. [PubChem CAS resolution](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/compound/name/7782-85-6/cids/JSON); [PubChem properties](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/compound/cid/6096963/property/MolecularFormula,MolecularWeight,InChI,InChIKey,CanonicalSMILES/JSON); [ChEBI parent](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/CHEBI:34683).

No exact ChEBI heptahydrate was found in the bounded live searches by CAS, exact names, and all returned heptahydrate/hydrogenphosphate/sodium-phosphate results; this is not a universal absence claim. CAS Common Chemistry was unavailable (page 403, API 401), so its contents were not used. NCI, FDA and PubChem independently support the CAS association. An ignored-file-inclusive scan of maintained ingredient YAML found no second current owner of NCIT:C61946 or CAS 7782-85-6. The 0.02 M stock is a distinct concentration-qualified preparation and must remain separate.

**Recommended implementation, after coordination:** promote the primary identifier and exact ontology grounding to NCIT:C61946 through the guarded writer and SSSOM receipt chain; retain the exact-form CAS as chemistry metadata; atomically move this record's existing rejection-ledger `mim_id` to NCIT:C61946 and correct its obsolete no-exact-term/CAS-only rationale. Keep CHEBI:34683 rejected as a unified identity. A new identifier alone grants no release approval.

**Current blocker is the explicitly protected unified rebuild in PR #914.** At inspected head `8dc2f266ebf72959a5d2f601d1c767c9138db44f`, #914 does not change this target YAML or its aggregate record hunk. The heptahydrate rejection-ledger row is unchanged diff context, so merely sharing that ledger path is not a conflict. However, #914 directly changes the `Na2HPO4 x 7 H2O` unified row from 19 to 28 occurrences while retaining the local identifier. This promotion would change that same row and hydrate aliases, requiring a coordinated unified rebuild and provenance update. Applying the primary without its ledger update would also fail Claw's identity-consistency guard. No record or generated mapping was changed in this audit.

The options are therefore (1) retain the evidence and defer application while #914 owns that rebuild, or (2) agree a coordinated atomic identity/ledger/receipt/unified update. Option 1 preserves the current non-overlap instruction. Prior #863, #334 and #459 decisions were inspected; this recommendation does not silently undo their hydrate boundaries. The broader finding `SEM:cb9ec35166086d936f70` also covers structure and provisional BUFFER evidence, which this identity decision cannot retire.

Evidence receipt: `output/sssom-curation-20261101T003435Z/audit875/` contains `audit875.json`, `audit875.md`, exact input hashes, primary-source response snapshots, bounded search results, prior issue comments, and the precise #914 diff. The audit is input to this batch's combined native review; it is not an independent release approval or a claim that all scientific review is complete. No paid research or provider credits were used.

title: Na2HPO4 x 7 H2O carries its own CAS 7782-85-6: decide §3 step 2 promotion (the #863 ledger row must move with it)
